summary: Decode KV offload now uses the existing DeepSeek-V4 composite HiCache host-pool/controller layout and carries SWA, C4/C128 compressed KV, indexer payload/scale, and C4 state sidecars through device-to-host, storage, and release accounting without inventing split K/V tensors. LMCache now preserves MHA and MLA layouts and resolves the existing grouped external-linker capability for composite pools, but the installed/current LMCache SGLang connectors still accept only k_pool/v_pool; SGLang therefore raises a precise NotImplementedError instead of misrepresenting the V4 layout.

tests.what_was_measured: 26 tests and 8 subtests passed, covering existing MHA/MLA decode-offload lifetime behavior, DeepSeek-V4 composite transfer enumeration/SWA translation, derived-sidecar ownership, and external-linker physical pool layout.

On one AMD Instinct MI355X with ROCm/HIP 7.2.26015, real device-to-pinned-host transfers for three paged sub-buffers and two ring-state sub-buffers matched independent torch indexing references byte-for-byte.
Repository formatting, lint, syntax, secret, and registered-test metadata checks passed for all changed source and evidence files.

remaining_limitations: LMCache dev at commit 05a013b29da78cf2321b9b46ec5039dde2fb0bb0 exposes LMCacheLayerwiseConnector and LMCacheMPConnector constructors with only k_pool/v_pool. Full LMCache V4 support requires LMCache to accept SGLang's grouped pool capability (pool names, per-layer mappings, page geometry, index translation, and multiple physical components) in both in-process and multiprocess registration/transfer paths.

No DeepSeek-V4 model weights or B300 system were available. The GPU test qualifies the actual composite host-transfer primitives and byte layout on MI355X, not DeepSeek-V4 model semantics, full PD serving, unified-KV mode, HiSparse, or LMCache daemon interoperability.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
